**What I found:** The plan would add a PluginRegistry so third parties can supply output formats. JSON is the only format, nobody has asked for a second one, and no third party is named. That makes it a plugin interface with one implementation and no second instance. Don't build it; the record calls this DROP. The skill rejects an abstraction outright when nobody can name a second instance.

**Why it matters:** The registry would sit between three commands (export, report, print) and the formatters. That is a new public extension API that would have to stay compatible, and nobody is using it. Each later change to formatter inputs would have to go through the registry and keep outside plugins working. Not building it costs nothing today, because no user is blocked.

**Do this first:**
1. Leave the export/report/print → JSON path as it is. Write down that this was dropped so it isn't proposed again without a named requester. That belongs in a ticket or the commit history, not a design doc.
2. Follow-up: when someone asks for a second format, add it next to JSON inside the CLI with no registry. Pull out a shared interface only when a third format appears or a named outside party needs to supply formats.

**What I did not check:**
- That JSON really is the only formatter. I didn't look at the code. Searching for formatter modules and how export/report/print call them would confirm it (Grep `format|serializ` across the CLI source).
- That nobody has asked for another format. This comes from you. Searching the issue tracker and support channels for format requests would confirm it.
